questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question: On a map, 1 inch represents 2.5 miles. A rectangular park appears on the map as 3 inches long and 2 inches wide. What is the actual area of the park, in square miles?
questions.explain: Convert each side first: 3 × 2.5 = 7.5 miles and 2 × 2.5 = 5 miles. The area is 7.5 × 5 = 37.5 square miles. Multiplying the map area (6) by 2.5 gives 15, which forgets that area scales by 2.5².

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question: A painter covers 120 square feet of wall in 45 minutes. At this rate, how many hours will it take the painter to cover 800 square feet?
questions.explain: 800 square feet is 800/120 = 20/3 times as much wall, so it takes (20/3)(45) = 300 minutes. That's 300/60 = 5 hours.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question: A train travels at a constant speed of 72 kilometers per hour. What is its speed in meters per second? (1 kilometer = 1,000 meters)
questions.explain: 72 km/h = 72,000 meters per 3,600 seconds = 20 meters per second. The value 1,200 is meters per minute, and 259.2 comes from multiplying by 3.6 instead of dividing.

questions.question: The price of an item is increased by 20%. The new price is then decreased by p%, which returns the item to its original price. What is the value of p?
questions.explain: After the increase, the price is 1.2 times the original. To get back, multiply by 1/1.2 = 5/6, which is a decrease of 1/6, or 16 2/3%. So p = 50/3 (16.66 or 16.67 also fit the answer box). It's not 20%, because the decrease applies to a larger amount.

questions.question: In 2020, a company had 240 employees, 35% of whom were women. In 2023, the company had 300 employees, 40% of whom were women. By approximately what percent did the number of women at the company increase from 2020 to 2023?
questions.explain: Women in 2020: 0.35 × 240 = 84. In 2023: 0.40 × 300 = 120. The increase is 36, and 36/84 ≈ 0.429, or about 43%. The 5% choice is the change in percentage points, not the percent change in the number of women.

questions.question: The number x is 150% of y, and y is 40% of z. The number x is what percent of z?
questions.explain: x = 1.5y and y = 0.4z, so x = 1.5(0.4z) = 0.6z, which is 60% of z. Percents of percents multiply; they don't add (190%) or subtract (110%).

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question: Every value in a data set is increased by 5. Which statement about the new data set is true?
choices: The mean increases by 5, and the standard deviation stays the same.
The mean and the standard deviation both increase by 5.
The mean stays the same, and the standard deviation increases by 5.
Neither the mean nor the standard deviation changes.
questions.explain: Adding 5 to every value shifts the whole data set up by 5, so the mean rises by 5. The values stay the same distance from one another and from the mean, so the spread, and therefore the standard deviation, doesn't change.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question: The mean of a student's 8 test scores is 85. After the lowest score is dropped, the mean of the remaining 7 scores is 88. What was the lowest score?
questions.explain: The 8 scores total 8 × 85 = 680. The remaining 7 total 7 × 88 = 616. The dropped score is 680 − 616 = 64.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question: A data set consists of the values 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, and x. The median of the data set is 5, and the mean is 6. What is the value of x?
questions.explain: A mean of 6 for 7 values means a total of 42. The known values add to 31, so x = 11. Check the median: in order, 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, the middle value is 5.

questions.question: Ten cards are numbered 1 through 10. Two cards are drawn at random, one after the other, without replacement. What is the probability that both cards show even numbers?
questions.explain: The first card is even with probability 5/10. After drawing one even card, 4 of the remaining 9 are even, so the second is even with probability 4/9. Multiply: (5/10)(4/9) = 20/90 = 2/9. The answer 1/4 assumes the card is put back.

questions.question: In a class of 30 students, 18 take Spanish, 12 take French, and 5 take both. If one student is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student takes neither Spanish nor French?
questions.explain: Students taking at least one language: 18 + 12 − 5 = 25 (subtract the 5 counted twice). So 30 − 25 = 5 take neither, and the probability is 5/30 = 1/6.

questions.question: In a survey of 400 adults, 160 own a dog. Of the dog owners, 60 also own a cat. Of the adults who do not own a dog, 90 own a cat. If one of the cat owners is chosen at random, what is the probability that this person also owns a dog?
questions.explain: Cat owners: 60 + 90 = 150, and 60 of them own a dog, so the probability is 60/150 = 2/5. The answer 3/8 (60/160) is the chance that a dog owner owns a cat, which reverses the condition.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question: A poll of randomly selected voters found that 52% support a ballot measure, with a margin of error of 4 percentage points. Which statement is most appropriate?
choices: It is plausible that less than half of all voters support the measure.
A majority of all voters definitely support the measure.
Exactly 52% of all voters support the measure.
Four percent of the voters polled gave inaccurate answers.
questions.explain: The plausible range is 52% ± 4, or 48% to 56%. That range includes values below 50%, so the poll can't show a majority. The margin of error describes sampling uncertainty, not false answers.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question: A forester randomly selected 120 trees from a forest of 3,000 trees and found that 18 of them had a fungal disease. Based on this sample, how many trees in the forest would be expected to have the disease?
questions.explain: The sample proportion is 18/120 = 0.15. Applying it to the forest: 0.15 × 3,000 = 450 trees.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question: A survey of 200 randomly selected students at Lincoln High School found that 70% of them favor a later school start time. Which conclusion is best supported by the survey?
choices: About 70% of all students at Lincoln High School likely favor a later start time.
About 70% of all high school students in the state favor a later start time.
Exactly 140 students at Lincoln High School favor a later start time.
Most teachers at Lincoln High School favor a later start time.
questions.explain: A random sample of Lincoln High students supports an estimate for Lincoln High students only, and as an estimate, not an exact count. Other schools in the state and teachers weren't sampled.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.question: In a study, volunteers chose for themselves whether to take a daily vitamin supplement. Over a winter, those who took the supplement reported fewer colds than those who did not. Why can't the researchers conclude that the supplement reduces colds?
choices: The participants were not randomly assigned to take or not take the supplement.
The study lasted for only one winter.
Some participants did not catch any colds.
The participants reported their own number of colds.
questions.explain: Because people chose for themselves, supplement takers may differ in other ways, such as being more health-conscious. Only random assignment allows a cause-and-effect conclusion. The other issues don't prevent that conclusion the way self-selection does.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.question: Researchers randomly selected 500 registered voters in a city and randomly assigned half of them to receive text-message reminders before an election. Turnout was significantly higher among those who received reminders. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
choices: Text reminders likely caused higher turnout among registered voters in the city.
Text reminders would raise turnout in every city in the country.
Text reminders are associated with turnout, but no causal conclusion is possible.
The results apply only to the 250 voters who received reminders.
questions.explain: Random assignment supports a causal conclusion, and random selection from the city's registered voters lets it apply to that whole group. It can't be extended to other cities, which weren't sampled.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.question: Data from several cities show that in months when ice cream sales are high, the number of drownings is also high. Which explanation best accounts for this relationship?
choices: Hot weather increases both ice cream sales and the number of people swimming.
Eating ice cream makes people more likely to drown.
Drownings cause people to buy more ice cream.
The relationship proves that ice cream sales should be limited in summer.
questions.explain: A third factor, hot weather, raises both ice cream sales and swimming (and so drownings). The data show only an association, so neither variable can be said to cause the other.

questions.question: A closed rectangular box has a volume of 360 cubic inches, a length of 10 inches, and a width of 6 inches. What is the total surface area of the box, in square inches?
questions.explain: Height = 360 ÷ (10 × 6) = 6 inches. Surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh) = 2(60 + 60 + 36) = 2(156) = 312 square inches.

questions.question: A right circular cone and a right circular cylinder have the same radius and the same volume. The height of the cylinder is 5 centimeters. What is the height of the cone, in centimeters?
questions.explain: Cone volume is (1/3)πr²h and cylinder volume is πr²(5). Setting them equal: (1/3)h = 5, so h = 15. A cone needs three times the height to hold as much as a cylinder with the same base.

questions.question: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 6, so that all four of its vertices lie on the circle. What is the area of the square?
questions.explain: The square's diagonal is a diameter of the circle: 12. A square with diagonal d has area d²/2 = 144/2 = 72. (Its side is 12/√2 = 6√2, and (6√2)² = 72.) The value 144 would be the area of a square with side 12.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = AC. The measure of angle B is (x + 15)°, and the measure of angle A is (2x)°. What is the measure of angle A?
questions.explain: Since AB = AC, the angles opposite those sides, B and C, are equal: both (x + 15)°. Then 2x + 2(x + 15) = 180, so 4x = 150 and x = 37.5. Angle A is 2x = 75°. (52.5° is angle B.)

questions.question: Two sides of a triangle have lengths 7 and 12. The third side has a length that is a whole number. What is the greatest possible length of the third side?
questions.explain: By the triangle inequality, the third side must be less than the sum of the other two: less than 7 + 12 = 19. The greatest whole number less than 19 is 18. (It must also be greater than 12 − 7 = 5.)

questions.question: In triangle PQR, point S lies on side PQ and point T lies on side PR, and segment ST is parallel to side QR. If PS = 4, SQ = 6, and ST = 5, what is the length of QR?
questions.explain: Because ST is parallel to QR, triangle PST is similar to triangle PQR. PQ = 4 + 6 = 10, so the scale factor is 10/4 = 2.5, and QR = 5 × 2.5 = 12.5. Using SQ instead of PQ gives 7.5, which compares the wrong segments.

questions.question: In a right triangle, one acute angle measures θ, and tan θ = 5/12. What is the value of sin θ?
questions.explain: tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 5/12, so the hypotenuse is √(25 + 144) = 13. Then sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 5/13. The choice 12/13 is cos θ.

questions.question: In right triangle ABC, angle C is a right angle, AC = 9, and cos A = 3/5. What is the length of BC?
questions.explain: cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse = AC/AB = 3/5, so 9/AB = 3/5 and AB = 15. Then BC = √(15² − 9²) = √(225 − 81) = √144 = 12.

questions.question: If sin(x°) = cos(40°) and 0 < x < 90, what is the value of x?
questions.explain: The sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement: sin(x°) = cos(90° − x°). So 90 − x = 40, and x = 50.

questions.question: The equation x2 + y2 + 4x − 10y = k represents a circle with radius 6 in the xy-plane. What is the value of k?
questions.explain: Complete the square: (x² + 4x + 4) + (y² − 10y + 25) = k + 4 + 25, so (x + 2)² + (y − 5)² = k + 29. The radius squared is 36, so k + 29 = 36 and k = 7.

questions.question: In a circle with radius 9, an arc has length 6π. What is the measure, in radians, of the central angle that intercepts this arc?
questions.explain: In radians, central angle = arc length ÷ radius = 6π/9 = 2π/3. (That's 120°.) The choice 54π multiplies instead of dividing.

questions.question: A circle in the xy-plane has its center at the origin and a radius of 13. The point (5, k) lies on the circle. Which of the following could be the value of k?
questions.explain: Points on the circle satisfy x² + y² = 169. With x = 5: 25 + k² = 169, so k² = 144 and k = 12 or −12. Of the choices, only −12 works.
